findings.claim: Slice 020K (CODEOWNERS wiring) is absent from both the §3 Track 1 ordering and the §9 autonomous-run-complete AC, despite WP-SCP-020 §4 declaring it an explicit PRECONDITION for 020D2.
findings.evidence: WP-SCP-020 §4 020K: 'Slice completes before 020D2 opens.' WP-SCP-020 §3 canonical ordering: '020J → 020K → 020D1 → …'. WP-SCP-022 §3 Track 1: '020J → 020D1 → 020D2' — 020K is nowhere in the chain. §9 AC states '8 PRs' ending at 020D2, omitting 020K.
findings.impact: 020D2 dispatched without 020K means CODEOWNERS is absent when branch protection is configured; required_approving_review_count and require_review_from_non_author settings in 020D2 reference a CODEOWNERS file that has not been committed. Slice will fail verify commands or leave main with malformed branch-protection state.
findings.mitigation: Insert 020K between 020J and 020D1 in §3 Track 1. Update §9 autonomous-run-complete AC to '9 PRs' with 020K in sequence: 020J → 020K → 020D1 → 020D2.

findings.claim: Slices 020E.b (post-protection canary) and 020E.c (waiver-suppression canary) are entirely absent from §3 Track 1. WP-SCP-020 §9 AC#3 requires all three canaries with committed fixture branches, gh pr view --json dumps, workflow-run-ids, and scripts/replay-canary.sh.
findings.evidence: WP-SCP-020 §3 canonical ordering places 020E.b and 020E.c between 020D2 and 020F. WP-SCP-020 §9 AC#3 explicitly names all three. WP-SCP-022 §3 post-USER-GATE-B sequence: 020E.a → 020F → 020G → 020H.1. 020E.b and 020E.c appear in no section of WP-SCP-022 — not in Track 1, not in out-of-scope §5, not in next-WP candidates §12.
findings.impact: WP-SCP-020 §9 AC#3 cannot close: no slice demonstrates the required check blocking a merge (020E.b) nor a waivers.json entry suppressing a deny (020E.c). scripts/replay-canary.sh has no assigned slice. The federation primitive ships without verified end-to-end enforcement evidence.
findings.mitigation: Insert 020E.b after 020D2 and 020E.c after 020E.b in the post-USER-GATE-B Track 1 sequence, before 020F. Assign scripts/replay-canary.sh authorship to one of the three canary slices. Correct the post-USER-GATE-B sequence to: 020E.a → 020E.b → 020E.c → 020F → 020G → 020H part 3 → 020H.1.

findings.claim: WP-SCP-022 §3 redefines slice IDs 020D2 and 020E.a with deliverables that contradict WP-SCP-020 §4, and the 'enable required status check on SCP main with enforce_admins=true' capability from WP-SCP-020 §4 020D2 does not appear anywhere in Track 1.
findings.evidence: WP-SCP-022 §3 item 8: '020D2 — Self-dogfood wrapper part 2: SCP CI green on the federated gate; selftest fixtures committed to repo.' WP-SCP-020 §4 020D2: 'Enable required status check on SCP main. scp/policy-check required on main with enforce_admins=true (closure of governance B-2).' WP-SCP-022 §3 item 12: '020E.a — First canary: FLA pin + branch protection.' WP-SCP-020 §4 020E.a: 'Pre-protection canary. Committed fixture branch canary/deliberate-violation-pre with deliberate Rego violation… cold-start + warm-start wall-clock times recorded (closure of m-devex-12). Evidence in canary-evidence.md.' WP-SCP-020 §3 canonical ordering places 020E.a before 020D2 (unprotected-branch demo), making it semantically incompatible with WP-SCP-022's post-USER-GATE-B placement after 020H releases. Scanning all 15 Track 1 items in WP-SCP-022 §3, no item corresponds to 'enable required status check on SCP main.'
findings.impact: The autonomous chain will: (a) dispatch '020D2' producing only selftest-green evidence — SCP main remains unprotected after the autonomous run, WP-SCP-020 §9 AC#2 permanently unmet; (b) dispatch '020E.a' as a FLA-pin canary producing incompatible evidence for WP-SCP-020 §9 AC#3; (c) never enable enforce_admins=true, leaving the governance B-2 closure absent from the audit record. Additionally, WP-SCP-022 §3 note on 020D1 states the wrapper pins to '@<commit-SHA-of-v1.0.0-rc.1>' but in the WP-SCP-022 ordering the rc.1 tag has not yet been cut when 020D1 runs (020H part 1 comes after USER-GATE-A), so the wrapper would pin to an untagged SHA.
findings.mitigation: Restore WP-SCP-020 §4 slice-ID definitions. Track 1 canonical sequence per WP-SCP-020 §3: 020J → 020K → 020D1 → 020H part 1 (cut rc.1 from 020D1 commit) → [USER-GATE-A if placed here, before pre-protection canary] → 020E.a (pre-protection canary on unprotected SCP branch) → 020H part 2 (promote to v1.0.0 after canary passes) → 020D2 (enable required check with enforce_admins=true) → 020E.b → 020E.c → [USER-GATE-B] → 020F → 020G → 020H part 3 → 020H.1. If the intent is to gate at a different point, amend WP-SCP-020 §3 via an explicit ordering amendment — the plan states 'slices may not be reordered without amending this plan' but does not record any amendment to the parent plan's ordering.

findings.claim: No programme-complete AC exists. §9 defines plan-complete and autonomous-run-complete but not programme-complete, leaving WP-SCP-020 §9 and WP-SCP-021 §9 without a closure path inside this programme.
findings.evidence: WP-SCP-020 §9 AC#1 requires all 19 slices (020A–020H.1) complete. WP-SCP-021 §9 AC#1 requires all slices 021A–021K complete. WP-SCP-022 §9 autonomous-run-complete covers Track 1 through 020D2 (8 slices) and Track 2 through 021E (4 slices). Post-gate slices — Track 1: 020H, 020E.a/b/c, 020F, 020G, 020H.1; Track 2: 021F, 021G — are listed in §3 but have no AC. §12 next-WP candidates names WP-SCP-024, WP-SCP-025, WP-SCP-022-proposal-queue, WP-SCP-023; no continuation WP for post-gate Track 1/2 completion. BACKLOG SCP-077 status 'in planning' has no transition condition to 'done.'
findings.impact: An orchestrator cannot determine when WP-SCP-022 as a whole is done. BACKLOG SCP-073 and SCP-075 remain 'in planning' with no defined closure condition inside the programme. Post-gate slices are stranded — listed in §3 but owning no AC and no named follow-up WP.
findings.mitigation: Add a third AC block: 'WP-SCP-022 is programme-complete when: all Track 1 slices through 020H.1 and all Track 2 slices through 021G are merged; WP-SCP-020 §9 and WP-SCP-021 §9 ACs are fully met; SCP-073 and SCP-075 status updated to done.' Alternatively, explicitly name a WP-SCP-022-continuation (or WP-SCP-022.post) in §12 covering the post-gate slices so the deferral is named, not implicit.

findings.claim: U-022-02 ('confirm personal-Pro account signed-commit configuration covers required-signed-commits on SCP main') is already answered by WP-SCP-020 §14 resolution of U-sec-2 and should be closed in this plan rather than deferred to slice 020J.
findings.evidence: WP-SCP-020 §14 U-sec-2 resolution: 'Personal GitHub Pro account ($4/mo). All four features supported on private repos.' WP-SCP-020 §6 lists the four features as: enforce_admins, tag-protection, required-signed-commits, required status checks. Required-signed-commits on main is explicitly one of the confirmed features. WP-SCP-022 §13 U-022-02 asks: 'need to verify the same configuration covers required-signed-commits on the SCP repo main branch' — this is precisely what U-sec-2 answered.
findings.impact: Leaving U-022-02 open causes the orchestrator to pause at slice 020J to gather information already in the repo. This unnecessarily consumes one of the five allowed fix rounds or triggers an unneeded user interruption for a question with a known answer.
findings.mitigation: Close U-022-02 in §13 with: 'CLOSED — answered by WP-SCP-020 §14 U-sec-2: personal GitHub Pro account supports all four features including required-signed-commits on main. No further verification needed before 020J.' Reference: WP-SCP-020 §14 U-sec-2 resolution.

findings.claim: USER-GATE-B is not referenced in §2 invariants, not in §9 ACs, and not in §3 'Autonomous run scope.' It exists only in the Track 1 slice ordering with no stated purpose beyond a one-line description.
findings.evidence: §2 Invariant #7: 'The chain does not blow through 020D2 → 020H or through 020H → 020E.a without explicit user acknowledgement' — names gate transitions by slice ID, not USER-GATE-B by name. §3 'Autonomous run scope': 'Track 1: through 020D2 then [USER GATE A]. Track 2: through 021E then [USER GATE C]' — USER-GATE-B absent. §9 ACs: 'User-gate A … and User-gate C … reached' — USER-GATE-B absent. §3 USER-GATE-B description: 'Pause before first canary. Confirms stability prereqs (see §7) before pinning a downstream repo' — §7 prereqs gate WP-SCP-024 estate cascade, not WP-SCP-022's own chain.
findings.impact: Without a §9 AC, the chain has no verifiable stop condition at USER-GATE-B. Without a §2 invariant naming it, nothing contractually prevents the chain from blowing through USER-GATE-B to 020E.a autonomously. The reference to '§7 stability prereqs' implies USER-GATE-B might belong to WP-SCP-024's scope, making its presence in WP-SCP-022 ambiguous.
findings.mitigation: Add USER-GATE-B to §2 Invariant #7 by name. Add a USER-GATE-B AC to §9 (e.g., 'User-gate B — stability prereqs §7 verified, user explicitly resumes before 020E.a canary'). In §3 'Autonomous run scope,' clarify that the autonomous run stops at USER-GATE-A; USER-GATE-B is a second pause within the post-gate resumption flow. If USER-GATE-B is actually a WP-SCP-024 boundary, move it to §12 next-WP candidates with an explicit note.

findings.claim: The plan does not specify which directory receives parent-plan deliverable artefacts (canary-evidence.md, branch-protection-log.md, release-signoff.md named in WP-SCP-020 §11) versus WP-SCP-022 dispatch artefacts (docs/reviews/WP-SCP-022/dispatches/<slice-id>/), leaving Codex executors without a deterministic output target.
findings.evidence: WP-SCP-022 §4.5: dispatch evidence lands at 'docs/reviews/WP-SCP-022/dispatches/<slice-id>/'. WP-SCP-020 §11: canary-evidence.md at 'docs/reviews/WP-SCP-020/canary-evidence.md' (020E.a/b/c), branch-protection-log.md at 'docs/reviews/WP-SCP-020/branch-protection-log.md' (020G), release-signoff.md at 'docs/reviews/WP-SCP-020/release-signoff.md' (020H part 2). WP-SCP-022 §4.1 dispatch-package instruction template 'Cites the parent slice text… includes explicit acceptance criteria' but does not specify the output directory convention for parent-plan deliverables. WP-SCP-021 §11 similarly names docs/reviews/WP-SCP-021/self-consume-evidence.md (021K) without clarification.
findings.impact: A Codex executor for 020G or 020H may write branch-protection-log.md or release-signoff.md into docs/reviews/WP-SCP-022/dispatches/020G/ instead of docs/reviews/WP-SCP-020/. WP-SCP-020 §9 ACs that reference these paths by name will fail closure checks.
findings.mitigation: Add to §4.1 and §4.5: 'Deliverables named in the parent plan §11 Review evidence section (e.g., canary-evidence.md, branch-protection-log.md, release-signoff.md) are written to docs/reviews/WP-SCP-020/ (or docs/reviews/WP-SCP-021/ as appropriate). WP-SCP-022 dispatch artefacts (dispatch-package.json, codex-stdout.txt, review JSONs, fixpoint.md) are written to docs/reviews/WP-SCP-022/dispatches/<slice-id>/. These directories are distinct and both must be populated.'

findings.claim: The 2026-05-31 D-021 atomic filing (touches DECISIONS.md) and the mid-May CT_AGENT_KEY_OPS ADOPT-001 §11.5 callout-removal (touches ADOPT-001) are not in the §8 risk register, despite both landing in the same wall-clock window as the autonomous chain running Track 1 slices that touch the same files.
findings.evidence: STATUS.md 'Next sensible actions': D-021 files on 2026-05-31, updating docs/DECISIONS.md. ADOPT-001 §11.5 callout-removal fires 'same week as CT flips DRAFT → Published' (target mid-to-late May 2026). WP-SCP-022 Track 1 post-USER-GATE-A includes 020H part 3 ('ADOPT-001 §12 appendix published') which edits ADOPT-001. WP-SCP-022 §8 risk register R-022-01 through R-022-08 does not include this risk. R-022-08 acknowledges the PR #35 / STATUS.md collision but not the DECISIONS.md or ADOPT-001 concurrent-edit scenario.
findings.impact: If the autonomous chain is running 020H part 3 (ADOPT-001 §12) while a parallel manual PR removes §11.5, the two PRs will produce a merge conflict on ADOPT-001. If D-021 files on 2026-05-31 while a completeness-review step for any slice proposes a new D-NNN, a numbering collision or DECISIONS.md merge conflict is possible.
findings.mitigation: Add R-022-09 to §8: 'Concurrent-edit risk — 2026-05-31 D-021 filing touches DECISIONS.md; mid-May ADOPT-001 §11.5 callout-removal touches ADOPT-001; both overlap the Track 1 post-gate autonomous window. Mitigation: (a) ADOPT-001 §11.5 removal is a separate one-line manual PR; it must rebase onto any open Track 1 implementation PR before merge. (b) D-021 adds a new row to DECISIONS.md using the reserved D-021 slot; no implementation slice proposes a D-NNN in the D-021 range. Orchestrator notes these two pending manual edits in the USER-GATE-A checkpoint briefing.'

findings.claim: ARCH-005 is listed in §1 Predecessors as a prerequisite 'for the rule-library work in 020C' but WP-SCP-020 §4 020C explicitly defines three and only three v1.0.0 rules (SCP-R-001/002/003), none of which reference ARCH-005 (canonical event-stream enforcement).
findings.evidence: WP-SCP-022 §1: 'ARCH-005 (PR #34, commit cccd042) — canonical event-stream rule, prerequisite for the rule-library work in 020C.' WP-SCP-020 §4 020C: 'Exactly 3 rules in v1.0.0 (BS-9 + A-N9 closure): SCP-R-001 (services.yml mode conformance), SCP-R-002 (waivers.json entry schema), SCP-R-003 (ADOPT-001 §11 vendoring-manifest marker presence).' WP-SCP-022 §2 'What this is NOT': 'Not a new rule. No rules added, removed, or amended. ARCH-005 is a prerequisite already on main' — this second reference classifies ARCH-005 as already-on-main context, contradicting the §1 claim that it specifically gates 020C.
findings.impact: Orchestrators reading §1 may gate 020C dispatch on ARCH-005 event-stream content that 020C's actual acceptance criteria do not require. Alternatively, if ARCH-005 is genuinely required for 020C (e.g., via a fourth Rego rule that enforces event-stream conformance), then WP-SCP-020's 'exactly 3 rules' invariant would be violated. Either way the claim as written is misleading.
findings.mitigation: Clarify or remove the '020C prerequisite' claim. If ARCH-005 is context (its rules are in the SCP registry and make the rule library more complete), restate §1 as: 'ARCH-005 (PR #34) — canonical event-stream rule, on main as context; not a gating prerequisite for 020C v1.0.0 rules.' If ARCH-005 does gate a specific acceptance criterion in 020C, name the criterion explicitly.

findings.claim: D-021 reservation is not noted in §10 or in DECISIONS.md, creating a risk that a Codex executor in the autonomous run assigns D-021 to a new decision during an implementation slice.
findings.evidence: DECISIONS.md table: D-020 (2026-04-18) then D-022 (2026-04-21) — D-021 row is absent with no comment. d019-may31-checkpoint.md §Pre-written amending decision draft and STATUS.md confirm D-021 is reserved for the 2026-05-31 checkpoint. WP-SCP-022 §10 enumerates D-026/D-027/D-028 without mentioning the D-021 gap.
findings.impact: A Codex executor implementing a slice that introduces a new decision (e.g., a completeness reviewer requests a decision record be added) may search DECISIONS.md for the next available D-NNN and assign D-021, colliding with the reserved draft and requiring manual cleanup before the 2026-05-31 filing.
findings.mitigation: Add a placeholder row to DECISIONS.md after D-020: '| D-021 | (reserved 2026-05-31) | Reserved — pre-written amending decision for mode.bearer_legacy checkpoint; see docs/reviews/WP-SCP-019/d019-may31-checkpoint.md | PENDING |'. Note the reservation in WP-SCP-022 §10.

findings.claim: §2 Invariant #7 describes gate transitions by slice-ID pairs ('020D2 → 020H', '020H → 020E.a') rather than by gate names, inconsistent with §3 notation and fragile if the ordering changes per C-022-03 mitigation.
findings.evidence: §2 Invariant #7: 'The chain does not blow through 020D2 → 020H or through 020H → 020E.a without explicit user acknowledgement.' §3 uses [USER GATE A] and [USER GATE B] as named pause points. The transition '020D2 → 020H' maps to USER-GATE-A; '020H → 020E.a' maps to USER-GATE-B. Neither gate name appears in §2.
findings.impact: If the Track 1 ordering is corrected per C-022-03 mitigation, the §2 Invariant #7 slice-ID references will become stale, requiring a second edit pass to keep the invariant accurate.
findings.mitigation: Replace §2 Invariant #7 with: 'The chain does not proceed past [USER-GATE-A] or [USER-GATE-B] without explicit user acknowledgement.'

findings.claim: U-022-01 specifies '$TBD per-slice budget, $TBD aggregate' with no default proposal, rendering the R-022-07 cost-cap mitigation unenforceable for the entire pre-USER-GATE-A run.
findings.evidence: §13 U-022-01: 'Default proposal $TBD per-slice budget, $TBD aggregate. Decided at user-gate A based on observed first-half spend.' §8 R-022-07: 'if cumulative review spend exceeds a per-WP cap (TBD with user at user-gate A), pause.' With no concrete cap value, the orchestrator has nothing to enforce before user-gate A.
findings.impact: A pathological slice that exhausts the 5-round fix budget produces unbounded review spend across up to 8 pre-gate slices × 5 rounds × 3 reviewers = up to 120 review dispatches before user-gate A, with no automatic halt.
findings.mitigation: Provide a default working figure in U-022-01: e.g., '$20 per-slice / $200 programme aggregate as default cap; confirmed or revised at user-gate A with observed spend substituted.' The orchestrator enforces the default and annotates the user-gate A briefing with actual vs. budget.

structured_review.summary: Three CRIT findings block merge. (1) 020K absent from Track 1 ordering and §9 AC despite being a declared PRECONDITION for 020D2. (2) 020E.b and 020E.c absent from programme entirely; WP-SCP-020 §9 AC#3 requires all three canaries. (3) 020D2 and 020E.a are silently redefined relative to WP-SCP-020 §4: WP-SCP-022 '020D2' = 'CI green / selftest fixtures' not 'enable required-status-check'; WP-SCP-022 '020E.a' = 'FLA pin + branch protection' not 'pre-protection SCP canary'; the enforce_admins=true enablement step does not appear anywhere in Track 1. Six MAJ findings: no programme-complete AC, U-022-02 already answered by WP-SCP-020 §14 U-sec-2, USER-GATE-B undefined in invariants and ACs, evidence-directory split between dispatch tree and parent-plan §11 paths unspecified, 2026-05-31 D-021 and mid-May ADOPT-001 concurrent-edit risks absent from risk register, ARCH-005 prerequisite for 020C unexplained against the three named v1.0.0 rules. Five MIN hygiene items. v0.2 required before merge per §9 AC#1 fixpoint rule.
